title: The Day a Nation Declared Its Independence
content:
On July 4, 1776, an important moment in history took place in Philadelphia.

At that time, the thirteen American colonies were under British rule. For many years, the people living in the colonies had problems with the British government. They were unhappy about taxes and wanted more freedom.

Many people began to believe that the colonies should become independent.

A group of representatives met to discuss the future of the country.

One of the most important documents in American history was written during this time: the Declaration of Independence.

Thomas Jefferson was the main author of the document. It explained why the colonies wanted to separate from Great Britain and become independent.

On July 4, 1776, the Continental Congress officially adopted the Declaration of Independence.

This did not immediately end the conflict. The American Revolutionary War continued for several years.

The colonies fought against Great Britain for their independence.

Finally, in 1783, the war officially ended, and the United States became an independent nation.

Today, July 4 is known as Independence Day in the United States.

Every year, Americans celebrate the day with fireworks, parades, music, family gatherings, and public events.

For many people, the Fourth of July is more than a holiday.

It is a day to remember an important moment in history:

The day thirteen colonies decided to imagine a new future and declare their independence.
